passages.text: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.
passages.sermon:
Christ has set us free.
He did this so that we can live in freedom.
Stand firm in this freedom.
Do not let yourselves become slaves again.
Do not take on the yoke of slavery once more.
passages.original: Τῇ ἐλευθερίᾳ ἡμᾶς Χριστὸς ἠλευθέρωσεν στήκετε οὖν καὶ μὴ πάλιν ζυγῷ δουλείας ἐνέχεσθε

passages.text: Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
\r\nI speak directly to you.
\r\nListen carefully.
\r\nIf you choose to be circumcised,
\r\nChrist will not benefit you at all.
passages.original: Ἴδε ἐγὼ Παῦλος λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε Χριστὸς ὑμᾶς οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει

passages.text: Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Galatia.
Paul testifies again.
He addresses every man who chooses circumcision.
If a man gets circumcised, he must obey the entire law.
He becomes obligated to keep all of the law.
passages.original: μαρτύρομαι δὲ πάλιν παντὶ ἀνθρώπῳ περιτεμνομένῳ ὅτι ὀφειλέτης ἐστὶν ὅλον τὸν νόμον ποιῆσαι

passages.text: You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to people who try to be justified by the law.
You try to become righteous by following the law.
You have been separated from Christ.
You have fallen away from grace.
passages.original: κατηργήθητε ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ οἵτινες ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοῦσθε τῆς χάριτος ἐξεπέσατε

passages.text: But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.
passages.sermon:
We are believers in Jesus Christ.
We live by faith.
God gives us His Spirit.
We wait with hope.
We hope for righteousness.
The Spirit helps us wait.
Our hope comes from faith.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς γὰρ Πνεύματι ἐκ πίστεως ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης ἀπεκδεχόμεθα

passages.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. All that matters is faith, expressed through love.
passages.sermon:
In Christ Jesus, circumcision has no value.
Uncircumcision also has no value in Christ Jesus.
Faith is what matters in Christ Jesus.
Faith works through love.
passages.original: ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ οὔτε περιτομή τι ἰσχύει οὔτε ἀκροβυστία ἀλλὰ πίστις δι’ ἀγάπης ἐνεργουμένη

passages.text: You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?
passages.sermon: You were following the truth well.\r\nSomeone stopped you from obeying the truth.\r\nYou are no longer following the truth because of this person.
passages.original: Ἐτρέχετε καλῶς τίς ὑμᾶς ἐνέκοψεν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ μὴ πείθεσθαι

passages.text: Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.
passages.sermon: God calls you.\r\nThis persuasion does not come from God.\r\nThis persuasion comes from another source.
passages.original: ἡ πεισμονὴ οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος ὑμᾶς

passages.text: A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.
passages.sermon:
A little leaven spreads through all the dough.
Leaven is a small ingredient.
Leaven changes the entire batch.
Even a small influence can affect everything.
passages.original: μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ

passages.text: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Galatians.
Paul trusted the Lord.
Paul felt sure about the Galatians.
Paul believed the Galatians would not accept any other teaching.
Someone was troubling the Galatians.
That person would face judgment.
It did not matter who that person was.
passages.original: ἐγὼ πέποιθα εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐν Κυρίῳ ὅτι οὐδὲν ἄλλο φρονήσετε ὁ δὲ ταράσσων ὑμᾶς βαστάσει τὸ κρίμα ὅστις ἐὰν ᾖ

passages.text: Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the believers.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul says, “If I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?”
Paul means that some people accuse him of preaching circumcision.
Paul is not preaching circumcision.
Paul is being persecuted because he preaches the cross of Christ.
If Paul preached circumcision, people would not be offended by the cross.
If that were true, the offense of the cross would be removed.
But the offense of the cross remains.
Paul is persecuted because he preaches the cross, not circumcision.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ δέ ἀδελφοί εἰ περιτομὴν ἔτι κηρύσσω τί ἔτι διώκομαι ἄρα κατήργηται τὸ σκάνδαλον τοῦ σταυροῦ

passages.text: As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Galatians.
\r\nPaul addressed the believers in Galatia.
\r\nSome people were agitating the believers.
\r\nThese agitators caused trouble among the believers.
\r\nPaul wished that these agitators would go even further and cut themselves off completely.
\r\nPaul expressed a strong desire that those who disturb the believers would remove themselves entirely.
passages.original: Ὄφελον καὶ ἀποκόψονται οἱ ἀναστατοῦντες ὑμᾶς

passages.text: For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers.
Paul calls them brothers.
God called you to live in freedom.
Do not use your freedom to serve your sinful desires.
Instead, serve each other with love.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς γὰρ ἐπ’ ἐλευθερίᾳ ἐκλήθητε ἀδελφοί μόνον μὴ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν εἰς ἀφορμὴν τῇ σαρκί ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης δουλεύετε ἀλλήλοις

passages.text: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
passages.sermon:
God gave the law to His people.
The law has many commands.
All the commands come together in one main rule.
This rule is simple.
Love your neighbor as you love yourself.
If you do this, you fulfill the whole law.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ πᾶς νόμος ἐν ἑνὶ λόγῳ πεπλήρωται ἐν τῷ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν

passages.text: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.
passages.sermon:
If you attack each other, you will harm each other.
If you keep hurting each other, you will destroy each other.
Be careful.
You may end up destroying one another.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἀλλήλους δάκνετε καὶ κατεσθίετε βλέπετε μὴ ὑπ’ ἀλλήλων ἀναλωθῆτε

passages.text: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Galatia.
Paul gives a command.
Paul says, “Walk by the Spirit.”
The Spirit is God’s Holy Spirit.
To walk by the Spirit means to live by the Spirit’s guidance.
Paul gives a result.
If you walk by the Spirit, you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
The flesh means sinful human desires.
If you follow the Spirit, you will not do what your sinful nature wants.
passages.original: Λέγω δέ Πνεύματι περιπατεῖτε καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν σαρκὸς οὐ μὴ τελέσητε

passages.text: For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.
passages.sermon:
The flesh desires things that are against the Spirit.
The Spirit desires things that are against the flesh.
The flesh and the Spirit are enemies.
They fight against each other.
Because of this, you do not do what you want.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τὸ δὲ Πνεῦμα κατὰ τῆς σαρκός ταῦτα γὰρ ἀλλήλοις ἀντίκειται ἵνα μὴ ἃ ἐὰν θέλητε ταῦτα ποιῆτε

passages.text: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit is the Holy Spirit of God.
The Holy Spirit leads believers in Jesus Christ.
If the Holy Spirit leads you, you follow Him.
If you follow the Holy Spirit, you do not live under the law.
The law does not rule over those led by the Spirit.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ Πνεύματι ἄγεσθε οὐκ ἐστὲ ὑπὸ νόμον

passages.text: The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery; idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions, and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
The acts of the flesh are clear.
The flesh means our sinful human nature.
These acts include sexual immorality.
They include impurity.
They include debauchery.
They include idolatry.
They include sorcery.
They include hatred.
They include discord.
They include jealousy.
They include rage.
They include rivalries.
They include divisions.
They include factions.
They include envy.
They include drunkenness.
They include orgies.
They include things like these.
I warn you about these acts.
I have warned you before.
Those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
passages.original: Φανερὰ δέ ἐστιν τὰ ἔργα τῆς σαρκός ἅτινά ἐστιν πορνεία ἀκαθαρσία ἀσέλγεια εἰδωλολατρία φαρμακεία ἔχθραι ἔρις ζῆλος θυμοί ἐριθεῖαι διχοστασίαι αἱρέσεις φθόνοι μέθαι κῶμοι καὶ τὰ ὅμοια τούτοις ἃ προλέγω ὑμῖν καθὼς προεῖπον ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες βασιλείαν Θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν

passages.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit produces good qualities in people.
These qualities are called the fruit of the Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit is love.
The fruit of the Spirit is joy.
The fruit of the Spirit is peace.
The fruit of the Spirit is patience.
The fruit of the Spirit is kindness.
The fruit of the Spirit is goodness.
The fruit of the Spirit is faithfulness.
The fruit of the Spirit is gentleness.
The fruit of the Spirit is self-control.
No law stands against these qualities.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ καρπὸς τοῦ Πνεύματός ἐστιν ἀγάπη χαρά εἰρήνη μακροθυμία χρηστότης ἀγαθωσύνη πίστις πραΰτης ἐγκράτεια κατὰ τῶν τοιούτων οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος

passages.text: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
passages.sermon:
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have a new identity.
They have crucified the flesh.
They have put to death their old sinful nature.
They have rejected its passions.
They have rejected its desires.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τὴν σάρκα ἐσταύρωσαν σὺν τοῖς παθήμασιν καὶ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις

passages.text: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.
passages.sermon: We live by the Spirit.\r\nLet us also walk by the Spirit.
passages.original: Εἰ ζῶμεν Πνεύματι Πνεύματι καὶ στοιχῶμεν

passages.text: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
passages.sermon:
We belong to Christ Jesus.
We must not become conceited.
We must not provoke one another.
We must not envy one another.
passages.original: μὴ γινώμεθα κενόδοξοι ἀλλήλους προκαλούμενοι ἀλλήλοις φθονοῦντες
